acceptanceCovered: SQLite/WAL ingestion state durably records canvas-scoped assets, jobs, deterministic units, chunks, attempts, cancellation, and lease generations so interrupted work resumes without rerunning completed units or accepting stale completion.

Enqueue is idempotent by immutable content SHA-256 and extractor version: unchanged content reuses the existing job/cache while a version change creates only new derived work without changing the raw asset identity.

Text, PDF, image-metadata, and table extraction is deterministic and bounded; malformed, encrypted, oversized, or unsupported inputs fail with typed sanitized states and never fabricate content or place raw bytes in model context.
The standalone bounded worker supports retry, backoff, cancellation, lease renewal, graceful shutdown, poison-unit terminal failure, and restart recovery with durable progress and failure reasons.

MCP ingestion tools expose enqueue, status, retry, cancel, and paginated chunk reads with centralized reader/trusted-service/operator authorization, loopback defaults, authenticated HTTP calls, canvas scope, and metadata-only denial audit.

Status and chunk responses are bounded, pure reads that expose trusted top-level data classification and provenance without local paths, credentials, capability URLs, raw bytes, or hidden extraction/mutation side effects.

Lab-agent permits only approved ingestion status/chunk reads, captures substantive bounded chunks as untrusted evidence, rejects mutation tools and arbitrary namespace suffixes, enforces inbound tool-result bounds, and applies Phase 5 locality before every subsequent provider call.

Canvus-MCP and lab-agent test, lint, type-check, parity, build, crash/restart, deduplication, authorization, cancellation, bounded-output, and no-write-after-denial regressions pass without live credentials or fake bypasses.

Architecture, operations, standards, roadmap, canonical specification, changelog, configuration, retention/capacity limits, extractor dependency boundaries, and the external-queue migration trigger accurately describe the implemented Phase 6 contract and remaining external gates.

H4 generic asset Content-Type propagation reaches text/CSV/TSV/JSON extractors.

H6 expired crash/reclaim attempts obey the poison ceiling.

M1 runtime close/unwind releases cache descriptor then SQLite; M2 valid leases renew and cancellation drains work; M3 benign token prose remains usable; M4 versions have service and database guards; M5 buffered downloads bind hashes to immutable paths.

Authorization, cross-canvas resource hiding, stale lease rejection, atomic chunk/unit commit, exact model namespace matching, mutation exclusion, locality failure closure, and Phase 7 untouched state.
